theme: 3 terms on hashing: the number a set uses to find an item, the object that mixes properties into that number, and two different values that end up with the same number

terms.definition: An integer made from a value that lets sets and dictionaries find it fast, and equal values always share it.
terms.example: Never save a Hash Value to disk, it changes every time the app launches.
terms.code:
let a = "swift".hashValue
let b = "swift".hashValue
print(a == b) // same value, same hash

terms.definition: The object passed to `hash(into:)` that mixes the properties you give it with `combine` into one hash value.
terms.example: Only feed `id` into the Hasher, that's enough to tell users apart.

terms.definition: When two different values get the same hash value; it still works, but lookups get slower.
terms.example: An empty `hash(into:)` makes every item a Hash Collision, so the set gets slow.

quizzes.question: In this code, what happens between two different `Bad` values, since they all get the same hash?
What do you call the object you feed properties into with `combine`?

video.title: Hash Value, Hasher & Hash Collision | Day 71
video.description:
Learn to explain hashing in Swift: Hash Value, Hasher & Hash Collision, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Hash Value - An integer made from a value that lets sets and dictionaries find it fast, and equal values always share it.
Hasher - The object passed to `hash(into:)` that mixes the properties you give it with `combine` into one hash value.
Hash Collision - When two different values get the same hash value; it still works, but lookups get slower.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.title: Swift Hash Value, Hasher & Hash Collision | Day 71
landscape.description:
Explain Hash Value, Hasher & Hash Collision in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
해시 값, Hasher, 해시 충돌 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Hash Value - An integer made from a value that lets sets and dictionaries find it fast, and equal values always share it.
한국어: 해시 값: 값으로 만든 정수로, 세트와 딕셔너리가 빠르게 찾을 때 씀. 같은 값은 항상 같은 해시 값을 가짐

Hasher - The object passed to `hash(into:)` that mixes the properties you give it with `combine` into one hash value.
한국어: Hasher: `hash(into:)`에 전달되어 `combine`으로 넣은 프로퍼티들을 하나의 해시 값으로 섞는 객체

Hash Collision - When two different values get the same hash value; it still works, but lookups get slower.
한국어: 해시 충돌: 서로 다른 두 값이 같은 해시 값을 갖는 것으로, 동작은 하지만 검색이 느려짐

In this video, Mina and Jake read a custom hash method, ask why it skips the name and find out what happens when two users share a hash, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.

dialogue.title: Same hash, different users

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, why does `User` write its own `hash` method?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It controls the Hash Value. Sets use it to find items fast.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A Hasher. `combine` feeds it properties and mixes them into one number.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: But it only gets `id`, not `name`. Is that a bug?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No. Giving the Hasher fewer fields than the equality check is fine.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So users with the same `id` but different names share a Hash Value?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, that's a Hash Collision. The set compares them for equality and keeps both.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Nothing breaks, but every Hash Collision makes lookups a bit slower.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. Equal users hash the same, but a matching hash doesn't mean equal.
Equal values always share the same Hash Value.
